title: Consumer lag keeps growing
brief: Order events go through a stream to consumers that write them to the database. Consumer lag grows all day and never comes down. Someone already doubled the consumers from 6 to 12, and it didn't help. Find out why and fix it.

variants.twist: A consumer crashes and the group rebalances: one consumer now reads two partitions. Set the consumers to 11 replicas. Does lag still stay down?

requirements: Consumers can batch: one that writes 10 events per DB call handles about 500 events/s (set capacity_rps to 500)
variants.twist: Events must stay in order per customer. Does adding partitions break that? What do you use as the partition key?

hints: Look at the stream's partitions and the consumer count. How many consumers are actually reading?
In a consumer group, each partition is read by one consumer at a time, so consumers beyond the partition count sit idle. Besides more consumers, what raises throughput per consumer?
Steady: work out the partition count where the consumers stop sitting idle. Growth: more partitions and consumers alone break the budget. What makes each consumer handle more messages per second?
_notes: Starter: client -> 8 services -> stream (6 partitions, $0.20) -> 12 workers (200/s) -> KV: $3.10. Only 6 read: drain 1.2k/s against 2k/s in, lag grows 800/s (12k after 15 s). 24 workers: still 6 readers, $4.30. 12 partitions: drain 2.4k/s, no lag, $3.10. Growth 6k/s: 30 partitions + 30 workers (unbatched) pass at $4.90 (over budget). Batched (500/s) 14 partitions + 14 workers: $3.30; 12 + 12 sits at exactly rho 1. Rebalance pauses and per-key ordering aren't modeled; discuss them in the twist. Checked in frontend/src/lessons/content.test.ts.
